issueCommentThread.body:
UAT: **focused-test-pass-1**

`nheroux-bit` cannot apply labels on this repo (`AddLabelsToLabelable` denied). Please add the `focused-test-pass-1` label to this issue.

Reproduces on **0.119.5** (Linux, Claude Code, npm global install) — same two symptoms, plus one downstream consequence worth recording.

```
$ directive session:start --session-id=host:claude:v1:...
[deft environment] os=linux; shell=bash; kind=default; path=/bin/bash; source=SHELL
fatal: Needed a single revision
exit 2
```

Fresh `git init` + `directive init`, zero commits. Same workaround: `git switch -c <branch>` then commit, after which `session:start` succeeds normally.

**Additional consequence:** because branch-protection refuses the initial commit to the default branch, and the workaround puts that commit on a feature branch, `master` is never created at all. The repo then has no default branch, and Directive itself reports this at session start:

```
[deft branch] Could not resolve a local default branch (`main` or `master`).
```

So the first-run state is not just "first commit needs a branch" — it is "the default branch does not exist," which persists silently until someone notices the warning. Recovering it meant `git branch master <scaffold-sha>` and merging the feature branches in; merge commits onto the default branch are not blocked by the gate, only direct commits are.

On a fresh `git init` the policy has no satisfiable starting move: there is no non-default branch to branch *from* until a default branch exists. Worth considering whether `directive init` should make the initial commit itself, or whether the branch gate should exempt an unborn HEAD.

Other findings from the same run: #4812, #4814.

Adoption blocker.

This is about Lifecycle: installing Directive, updating it, and getting one clear next step when something looks wrong. It also covers whether the version someone thinks they installed is the version that is actually running.

What a new person hits: They create a brand-new empty project, the normal way to try a tool, and starting a session dies because the folder has no commits yet. Making that first commit on the main branch is also blocked.

Why that ruins the product for them: The getting-started path is a dead end. They did the ordinary thing and the product will not begin.

How likely: High for anyone who tries Directive in a new folder, which is the usual first experiment.

### 1 A feature-branch commit on an unborn HEAD is a starting move

sharpens-framing

Evidence. Two mechanisms in the refutation target hold at eec15b57b142591c99bd8a68c13dda573f1c03aa.

Mutation session:start returns code 2 when git HEAD does not resolve. gitHead in packages/core/src/session/git.ts runs rev-parse --verify HEAD and returns a null head on a nonzero status. The mutation path in packages/core/src/session/session-start.ts returns code 2 and prints that stderr when gitHeadValue is null. The read-only return at line 1525 is earlier and is a different command. On this host, git 2.55.0.windows.5 in an empty git init -b main prints "fatal: Needed a single revision". That is the fatal line comment 5747710278 recorded with exit 2 on Linux under @deftai/directive 0.119.5. The installed engine @deftai/directive-core@0.119.5 still returns code 2 from that branch. This host's command status reports 1 for a node process that exits 2, which I checked by running a two-exit node process, so that collapsed status is not the measurement.

The branch gate refuses the unborn default branch. currentBranch uses symbolic-ref --short HEAD. On that empty repo the symbolic ref was main, so the detached-HEAD pass does not apply. evaluate refuses a default branch when direct commits are disallowed. createSkeleton writes a PROJECT-DEFINITION with no allowDirectCommitsToMaster flag, so resolvePolicy is default-fail-closed with a null error, and evaluate takes the #747 refusal. With no definition at all, the same function refuses as well. Installed @deftai/directive 0.119.5 printed "PROJECT-DEFINITION cannot be resolved" on an unborn main repo.

The closing clause of the refutation target does not hold. A starting move already exists, and the gate allows it.

On a second empty repo I ran git switch -c chore/deft-init before any commit. symbolic-ref then printed chore/deft-init. rev-parse --verify HEAD still printed "fatal: Needed a single revision". directive verify:branch --project-root on that repo exited 0 and printed "feature branch 'chore/deft-init' -- proceeding." evaluate returns that pass for every non-default branch before it reads policy, so a missing definition does not change it. On another unborn chore/deft-init, git commit --allow-empty created root commit 118713ecf72beac5be1295a982a490946fdf65bf. git branch listed only chore/deft-init. rev-parse --verify HEAD then printed that commit. main was never created.

That is the recovery evaluate already prints (git switch -c feat/<name>) and the recovery printCommitGuidance already prints when init has paths to commit (git switch -c chore/deft-framework-upgrade, then commit). runInitDeposit prints that guidance before printNextSteps says to open the assistant. The issue body and comment 5747710278 both record that this commit is what made session:start succeed. After HEAD resolves, the null-HEAD return does not run. A missing local main or master is the defaultBranchSync warning in session-start.ts, and that warning is not an exit 2.

Failure mode. A successor lean that binds "there is no satisfiable starting move" spends the remedy on inventing a commit path. The gate already accepts a commit on a branch other than main or master, including while that branch has no parent commit. An unborn-HEAD exemption on the default branch, which comment 5747710278 floats, would widen default-branch commit authority to fill a scarcity the gate does not have. Init creating the first commit would be further product work on top of a move that already lands.

Disposition. Bind the narrower pain. Mutation session:start returns 2 while rev-parse --verify HEAD fails. verify:branch refuses the first commit on the unborn default branch. A feature-branch commit created with git switch -c on that unborn HEAD is already allowed, and that commit is what makes HEAD resolvable. P1 in the gate stamp already says the unborn default branch has no satisfiable first commit. That sentence can stand. The refutation-target's last clause, that there is no satisfiable starting move, cannot be the bound cause.

Road not taken. Classing the whole sentence blocks-the-design would unbind a P1 the gate stamp already states as the default-branch commit, and that narrower sentence survived the check. What flips this finding to blocks-the-design: verify:branch refusing chore/deft-init while rev-parse --verify HEAD still fails.

Steelman. The strongest reading of "no satisfiable starting move" is a move a new person can recognize from Next steps. Next steps says to open the assistant. Commit guidance is framed as an upgrade PR, and "create a feature branch" can be read as if a default-branch commit had to exist first. That is a statement problem in the init dump. The git operation itself succeeds. That is what this check measured.

The recorded target is the failure report. It leaves commit authority where it is. I am not adopting the unborn-HEAD exemption in comment 5747710278. That exemption would change who may commit on the default branch. This round's evidence is that the feature-branch pass already exists.

### 2 Read-only session:start does not resolve HEAD

footnote

runReadOnlySessionStart returns code 0 with ready true and does not call gitHead. The posture check at session-start.ts:1525 returns before the null-HEAD exit. The reporters ran the default mutation command. Read-only alignment leaves that command on the exit-2 path, and it leaves the bound pain as stated in finding 1.

### Bound remedy keeps both P1 conjuncts

blocks-the-design

Stop 1 write-back 5781763381 owns P1. The gate stamp is session:start exit 2 on a repository with no commits, together with no satisfiable first commit on the unborn default branch.

Successor lean 5782025773 harvests a Bound remedy that keeps both conjuncts. Bullet 1 keeps the mutation session:start return of 2 while `rev-parse --verify HEAD` fails. Bullet 3 names a commit on a different branch. Bullet 6 says Next steps leave that move unstated. The harvest contains no change that makes either conjunct false. The read-only return at line 1525 is an earlier, different command. `evaluate` in `packages/core/src/branch/evaluate.ts` returns exit 0 for a non-default branch before `resolvePolicy`. On `main` or `master` it reads policy. `createSkeleton` writes no `plan.policy.allowDirectCommitsToMaster` flag. `resolvePolicy` then returns default-fail-closed with a null error, and `evaluate` takes the exit 1 refusal. A missing definition is the earlier exit 2 path (`PROJECT-DEFINITION cannot be resolved`). `.githooks/pre-commit` runs `verify:branch`.

On this host, an empty `git init -b main` made `rev-parse --verify HEAD` print `fatal: Needed a single revision` (exit 128). `git switch -c chore/deft-init` on that unborn HEAD, then `git commit --allow-empty`, created root commit `c388857ed52c100b352720094e0e21383ca8ebb1`. `git branch --list` showed only `chore/deft-init`. That temp repo had no deft hook, so the commit shows git accepts the root commit. The default-branch refusal is the `evaluate` path above. `printNextSteps` step 1 tells the reader to open the assistant. When `printCommitGuidance` has paths, it prints `git switch -c chore/deft-framework-upgrade` framed as an upgrade PR, and `runInitDeposit` prints that guidance before the CLI prints Next steps.

Failure mode. Binding this lean treats P1 as covered. The zero-commit mutation command still returns 2. The first commit on the unborn default branch stays fail-closed. A builder who implements the harvest keeps both outcomes. Round-1 critic 5781995754 said the gate-stamp sentence can stand. This lean accepts that sharpening and still carries the relief cite.

Disposition. The lean cannot bind as written. Post a retraction map for P1, then print Handoff. This audit is not relief. A Next-steps sentence that names the feature-branch commit leaves both conjuncts in place, so that edit does not clear this finding.

Authority. The harvest leaves default-branch commit authority where `evaluate` already puts it. The feature-branch pass is that existing early return, before policy, so it is not a new bypass of the default-branch gate. The unborn-HEAD exemption in comment 5747710278 would widen who may commit on `main` or `master`. This audit does not adopt that exemption. The harvest changes no envelope, identity, or shared state.

Road not taken. Treating the unstated Next-steps line as a framing fix would send a new bind lean whose harvest still preserves exit 2 and the default-branch refusal, and the relief cite would stay false. This finding becomes framing-only if a later Stop 1 pain text is only the unstated move, with exit 2 and the default-branch refusal outside that id. It becomes a footnote if a later Bound remedy makes one of those two conjuncts false.

Steelman. The charter is refutation, and the refutation-target's last clause is false. The feature-branch root commit above is a starting move, and once HEAD resolves the null-head return does not run. The tester's expected result allows a required commit when the docs say so before opening the assistant. That reading treats P1 as the claim that no move exists. The gate stamp names the unborn default branch, and this lean's harvest keeps that commit refused.

## Tester 1 (Codex / Windows / @deftai/directive@0.119.1)

**Checks:** C5, C6, C10
**Defect:** 12

### Expected
After `directive init` on a new clone, the agent session can start. If a commit is required, init or README says so before "open your AI assistant".

### What happened
`deft session:start` → `fatal: Needed a single revision because this repository has no initial commit`. First `git commit` on `main` refused by branch-protection (#747, default-fail-closed). Feature branch required; only mentioned inside the init dump. Workaround: `git switch -c chore/deft-init` then commit `855e9ad`.

### Evidence
git commit error; session:start fatal; init never committed.

### Environment
Empty clone + init, zero commits. Directive 0.119.1.
